claims.text: The as-cast alloy has a heterogeneous, relatively coarse grain structure.
The as-cast alloy has an uneven precipitate distribution.
Controlled annealing can refine the grain size.
Controlled annealing can promote uniformly distributed nanoscale precipitates.
A processing window exists in which precipitation and grain refinement occur without detrimental phase segregation or excessive grain growth.
Reduced grain size and coherent nanoscale precipitates modify magnetic exchange-interaction pathways.
Annealing fine-tunes the balance between localized and long-range magnetic exchange interactions.
Fine-tuning magnetic exchange interactions lowers the magnetic-energy barrier for spin reorientation at low applied fields.
Lowering the spin-reorientation energy barrier increases the low-field magnetocaloric response.
Lowering the spin-reorientation energy barrier reduces magnetic hysteresis.
The annealing-induced microstructure supports faster thermal recovery.
The annealing-induced microstructure maintains mechanical integrity.
Optimally annealed samples will have a greater magnetic entropy change at modest applied fields than the as-cast baseline.
Optimally annealed samples will have narrower magnetization hysteresis loops than the as-cast baseline.
Optimally annealed samples will retain rapid heat exchange relative to the as-cast baseline.
Optimally annealed samples will retain robust mechanical properties relative to the as-cast baseline.
The hypothesis should cease to hold when annealing causes excessive grain growth, substantial phase segregation, or brittle-phase formation.
